# TT

> One calendar for the two of you: plans, anniversaries and day counts, with a notification when your partner changes something. Works in the browser, no app store needed. Free and open source.

TT is a web app (a PWA): it runs in the browser on iPhone, Android and computers and can be added to the home screen. It is free and open source (MIT, https://github.com/jowon-kim/tt-calendar) with no ads and no paid features; anyone can run their own copy, so the calendar stays in their own database. Available in English, 한국어, 日本語, 简体中文, Español, Français, Deutsch, Português (Brasil), Русский.

## What it does

- Mine, yours, ours: Each plan belongs to one of you, or to both — shown in its own colour.
- Your partner hears about it: When one of you adds, edits or deletes a plan, the other gets a notification. Your own changes never ping you.
- Reminders that just arrive: A “starting soon” note 30 minutes to an hour before timed plans, and one summary of the day at 8 in the morning.
- Days together, counted: Enter the day you met: 100 days, 200 days and every anniversary appear on the calendar, with a countdown to each.
- Your photos on it: Add up to 30 photos and they turn up beside plans and on empty days.
- Your language, your holidays: Nine languages, public holidays for nine countries, and your own time zone.

## Questions

- Is TT free? Yes. TT is free and open source (MIT), with no ads and no paid features. You can run your own copy, so your calendar stays in your own database.
- Do we need to download it from an app store? No. TT runs in the browser on iPhone, Android and computers. Adding it to the home screen makes it open like an app, and that is also how notifications work on iPhone.
- Does it work on iPhone? Yes. Open it in Safari, tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”. On iOS 16.4 and later it can send notifications once it is on the home screen.
- How do I invite my partner? In Settings, make an invite link and send it. When your partner signs up through it, you share the same calendar. Each of you keeps your own account.
- What do you collect? Your Google account number and email address (to know it is you), and what you put in the calendar: plans, names, dates and photos. No password. You can delete your account at any time from Settings.
- What if one of us deletes their account? The calendar stays with the other person. When both of you have left, the plans and photos are deleted.
